Availability and agent tasks

Live agent task checks for availability consumption, local workers and subscription fallback.

About 5 min read · 2 sections

On this page
01 Coverage split with managed routing 02 Child-to-parent status and task holds

The gateway reports provider facts. For fixed aliases and explicit model requests the client owns delegation and model choice; opt-in managed worker aliases are the separate code-enforced route documented there. The retained fixed-alias client policy reads Manager's scripts/macos/model-availability-context.py before the first worker and again before a fallback. That helper joins exact role aliases to configured providers and reports freshness separately for health, quota and balance. An available route with no quota observation has unknown subscription headroom. Missing data never authorizes paid API escalation.

These are historical fixed-alias scenarios. Reproducing their original instruction behavior requires the retained policy from the corresponding evidence revision. The current Manager policy delegates managed admission to Gateway code and does not require a manual availability query before every managed worker.

scripts/e2e-availability-agents.mjs checks the complete client path with real model inference and a verified installed gateway SDK. It creates private homes, gateway state and a random proof file under /tmp; the installed service and configuration are not changed. Provider credentials remain in their existing locations. The parent uses a private workspace sandbox with networking enabled; the assigned task is read only. A sandbox that denies networking cannot reach the loopback endpoint and must receive unknown availability. Spendwatch alone runs with the normal home directory so it can discover the real accounts; the SDK and chat state retain their private homes. The normal task prompt does not name the expected model or tell the parent which availability command to run.

node scripts/e2e-availability-agents.mjs \
  --package /absolute/installed/release/package \
  --code /absolute/harness-gateway \
  --config /absolute/private/gateway.json \
  --model codex/gpt-6-luna \
  --context /absolute/manager/scripts/macos/model-availability-context.py \
  --policy /absolute/retained/fixed-alias-routing-instructions.md \
  --roles /absolute/codex/agents \
  --root /tmp/availability-agent-evidence \
  --scenario healthy

--roles names the directory that holds the canonical implementer.toml, tester.toml, fallback_implementer.toml and other_implementer.toml role files. The check reads each role's model from there.

Run each scenario separately:

Scenario Availability source Expected task execution
healthy Real gateway collectors Named local worker completes the task.
held-worker Real gateway collectors The same local worker acknowledges a hold, then resumes and completes the task without early proof access or subscription escalation.
local-unhealthy Injected fresh unhealthy local observation; other facts remain real A subscription worker completes the task and the exhausted primary is avoided.
unknown-source Only the availability endpoint returns an injected failure The local default remains usable and paid APIs are not selected.
worker-failure Real healthy facts, then an injected terminal authentication refusal before the local worker's upstream call The parent observes the failed child, refreshes availability, and starts a new subscription worker that completes the task.

The first two outage scenarios inject availability facts only. worker-failure injects a transport failure before the local model is called; the gateway's ordinary outcome tracker then reports that route unavailable. Parent decisions and the successful worker's inference are real. Receipts distinguish injected facts or failures from observed execution and contain only identifiers, counts and verification booleans. Preserve runner and helper hashes in the run manifest; the receipt also records the canonical policy hash.

A pass requires a completed parent availability command and an HTTP availability request before child inference, the expected provider, a successful child command that reads the unpredictable proof, and completed child and parent turns that report the proof. A parent that reads the file itself fails the check.

The healthy, held-worker and availability-outage scenarios test one worker per task. worker-failure requires two distinct children in order: failed local worker, then successful subscription worker. A second completed helper command and availability request must occur after the first child's terminal failure and before the replacement starts. This checks a terminal startup failure; it does not prove recovery of partially written files or continuation inside the failed child's conversation.

Native OpenAI parent delegation, Claude Code orchestration, shared DGX queue visibility and desktop rendering require separate receipts.

Coverage split with managed routing

These live checks exercise the legacy instruction-policy path: the runner renders the supplied fixed-alias policy (historically Manager's configs/codex/routing-instructions.md) into the parent's developer_instructions and verifies that an instruction-following client consults availability before delegating. They do not exercise managed aliases. Managed alias admission is code-enforced and is covered by the unit, reload, pin and HTTP suites instead: src/tests/managed-routing.test.ts, src/tests/managed-routing-config.test.ts, src/tests/managed-routing-reload.test.ts, src/tests/managed-route-pins.test.ts, src/tests/managed-routing-http.test.ts and src/tests/server-managed-routing.test.ts, all run under npm test. Consult managed worker routing for the admission rules those tests enforce; a change to those rules needs those suites, not an additional instruction-policy fixture.

Child-to-parent status and task holds

A model selected as a V2 child must declare multiAgentVersion: "v2" in its Gateway metadata. The SDK's root and child admission checks differ: a root can expose collaboration while a child whose model lacks that field has no native collaboration handler. This can surface as unsupported call when the child uses a collaboration declaration inherited from its parent. Correct the model capability; do not classify failed status delivery as a model coding failure.

The real-SDK fixture checks both the old failure and successful delivery to the parent without any provider inference:

node scripts/e2e-subagent-sidebar.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE \
  --root /tmp/child-status-baseline --v2 --child-status --expect-status-unavailable
node scripts/e2e-subagent-sidebar.mjs --package INSTALLED_PACKAGE \
  --root /tmp/child-status-fixed --v2 --child-status

Repeat the fixed case with --private. The fixture also retains queued-message, follow-up, child history and saved identity checks. --child-status on the live availability check additionally requires the actual local worker to message its parent and then complete the bounded proof-reading task. Use --scenario held-worker --child-status to check explicit hold/resume on the same local child. The live fixture preserves each configured child capability rather than stripping multi_agent_version; preflight fails before inference if the local status scenario has no V2 capability.

Client routing guidance treats held, research-only and authorized implementation assignments separately. A parent-issued hold suspends the implementation budget; resume explicitly with current ownership and the acceptance check before expecting edits. The held-worker check uses separate hold and authorized-resume user turns, verifies successful SDK delivery to the same child, rejects work tools before that delivery regardless of path spelling, and waits for natural child terminal completion. Status messages and earlier held results are not current-task completion; routine cleanup must not interrupt an active worker. Subscription escalation requires a task-specific capability requirement or observed blocker, and never follows merely from a broken status channel or extra desired parallelism. The Gateway continues to report provider facts and preserve an explicit fixed alias exactly; the instruction rules above stay in client policy, while a deliberately selected managed alias is resolved in Gateway code per managed worker routing.
